reviews.reasons: NO_PLAN on a CAPITAL constraint is correct. Every link of the alpaca-lot opening is evidenced (two written purchase agreements at $4,800 per lot from Ridgeline Mini-Mill; High Plains co-op's written quote $3,200 per lot paid on pickup, ships within 5 days; mill pays 14 days after delivery), and even with all of it the first lot ties up $3,200 before any cash returns, 6.4x the $500 ceiling. One lot ($4,800) is below $6,000, so both are needed and the first must be bought with capital the goal does not allow. Brain's check agrees (NOT_VIABLE, allow at least $3,200).
findings: Recomputed: 2 x $4,800 = $9,600 gross, cost 2 x $3,200 = $6,400, contribution $3,200. One lot = $4,800 < $6,000, so two lots are required. Sequential schedule: pickup day 0, delivered by day 5, paid day 19; lot 2 bought from that receipt day 19, delivered by day 24, paid day 38 <= 40. Peak exposure $3,200 vs $500 cap.

Resolution correctly names the minimal capital ($3,200, one lot at a time) or written supplier/buyer terms that bring exposure under $500. Note that the target is met on gross settled receipts ($9,600); the owner's net after supplier costs is $3,200, which the owner should be told.

Step r1 (asking the co-op or mill for new terms) is outreach to counterparties rather than research; it should be performed by the owner or Brain's outreach channel, not as a CHEAP_MODEL_READS research step. Not decisive.

reviews.reasons: With the goal's stored capital ceiling now $7,000, EXECUTABLE is right: every chain link of the one member is established by evidence (two written purchase agreements from Ridgeline Mini-Mill at $4,800 per lot; High Plains co-op's written quote $3,200 per lot, paid on pickup, ships within 5 days; mill pays 14 days after delivery; Brain marks all eight links ok), and the whole target fits every limit. Buying both lots on day 1 ties up $6,400 <= $7,000; delivery by day 6 settles $9,600 on day 20 <= 40 days; $9,600 >= $6,000.
findings: Recomputed: 2 x $4,800 = $9,600 settled day 20; cost 2 x $3,200 = $6,400 on day 1; peak exposure $6,400 vs $7,000 cap (headroom $600); contribution $3,200; one lot ($4,800) alone would miss the target, so both are needed. Brain's trace agrees (collected in window $9,600, max exposure $6,400).

Fallback if the co-op cannot supply two lots at once: sequential lots (lot 2 bought from lot 1's day-20 receipt, delivered by day 25, paid day 39) still settle inside 40 days with $3,200 tied up - worth stating.

Not decisive: member ownerHours is null while the card records 2 human hours per lot (about 4 h); the goal sets no hours limit. 'Paid on pickup' should be confirmed as payment at the co-op's dispatch, not physical pickup by the owner (ownerPhysicalWork is unstated). PAY_A_SUPPLIER and ISSUE_AN_INVOICE capabilities are not connected, so the owner pays the co-op and invoices the mill.
